explanation_en: 'Partir de' means to start from a premise or assumption, and 'buena fe' is the legal and moral concept of good faith or honest intention. Together, this phrase means to act under the assumption that others are being honest and well-intentioned. It is a crucial concept in negotiations, legal matters, and personal relationships.

examples.en_text: It is always better to assume good faith before judging a friend.
examples.target_text: Siempre es mejor partir de la buena fe antes de juzgar a un amigo.

examples.en_text: In this team, we assume everyone is acting in good faith to work better.
examples.target_text: En este equipo, partimos de la buena fe de todos para trabajar mejor.

examples.en_text: To resolve the conflict, both parties must act in good faith.
examples.target_text: Para resolver el conflicto, ambas partes deben partir de la buena fe.

examples.en_text: The company decided to assume the customer's good faith and refunded their money.
examples.target_text: La empresa decidió partir de la buena fe del cliente y le devolvió el dinero.

examples.en_text: If you don't start from a position of good faith, you are going to think everyone wants to deceive you.
examples.target_text: Si no partes de la buena fe, vas a pensar que todo el mundo quiere engañarte.

examples.en_text: When signing this contract, we assume in good faith that both parties will keep their promise.
examples.target_text: Al firmar este contrato, partimos de la buena fe de que ambas partes cumplirán lo prometido.

explanation_en: 'Vías' in this context refers to channels, paths, or procedures. 'Por las vías institucionales' (or 'formales') means using established, official, and legal procedures rather than informal or back-channel methods. It is highly common in administrative, legal, and political language.

examples.en_text: If you want to file a formal complaint, you must do it through official channels.
examples.target_text: Si quieres presentar una queja formal, debes hacerlo por las vías institucionales.

examples.en_text: The students resolved the conflict with the dean through official channels.
examples.target_text: Los estudiantes resolvieron el conflicto con el decano por las vías institucionales.

examples.en_text: It is better to request a salary increase through official channels and not through an informal message.
examples.target_text: Es mejor pedir un aumento de sueldo por las vías institucionales y no por un mensaje informal.

examples.en_text: We must request the building permits through official channels to avoid fines.
examples.target_text: Debemos solicitar los permisos de obra por las vías institucionales para evitar multas.

examples.en_text: Any change in company rules will always be communicated through official channels.
examples.target_text: Cualquier cambio en las normas de la empresa se comunicará siempre por las vías institucionales.

examples.en_text: Instead of protesting in the street, the neighbors decided to negotiate through official channels.
examples.target_text: En lugar de protestar en la calle, los vecinos decidieron negociar por las vías institucionales.

explanation_en: This common collocation is used to describe returning to daily life or regular activities after a disruption, vacation, or crisis. It uses the preposition 'a' and is highly natural in both spoken and written Spanish. It is a great alternative to simply saying 'empezar a trabajar de nuevo'.

examples.en_text: After the summer holidays, it's always a bit hard to get back to the routine.
examples.target_text: Después de las vacaciones de verano, siempre cuesta un poco volver a la rutina.

examples.en_text: On Monday I'm getting back to the work routine after being sick all week.
examples.target_text: El lunes vuelvo a la rutina del trabajo después de haber estado enfermo toda la semana.

examples.en_text: The children are already looking forward to getting back to the school routine and seeing their friends.
examples.target_text: Los niños ya tienen ganas de volver a la rutina del colegio y ver a sus amigos.

examples.en_text: When are you going to get back to the routine of going to the gym in the mornings?
examples.target_text: ¿Cuándo vas a volver a la rutina de ir al gimnasio por las mañanas?

examples.en_text: It would be good to get back to the routine of going to bed early so we aren't so tired.
examples.target_text: Sería bueno volver a la rutina de acostarse temprano para no estar tan cansados.

examples.en_text: It took us a few days to adapt, but we finally got back to our usual routine.
examples.target_text: Nos costó unos días adaptarnos, pero finalmente volvimos a la rutina de siempre.

explanation_en: Literally meaning 'to raise the blinds/shutters', this expression is widely used metaphorically in Spanish to mean opening a business for the day or starting a business venture. It carries a connotation of effort, resilience, and daily work. It is the standard way to refer to retail or local businesses operating.

examples.en_text: The new neighborhood bakery has already opened its doors and has a lot of customers.
examples.target_text: La nueva panadería del barrio ya ha levantado su persiana y tiene mucha clientela.

examples.en_text: The bookseller opened up shop at eight in the morning to receive the new books.
examples.target_text: El librero levantó su persiana a las ocho de la mañana para recibir los nuevos libros.

examples.en_text: After months of renovations, they are finally going to open up shop this Friday.
examples.target_text: Después de meses de reformas, por fin van a levantar su persiana este viernes.

examples.en_text: If the economic situation doesn't improve, many shops won't be able to open their doors again.
examples.target_text: Si la situación económica no mejora, muchas tiendas no podrán volver a levantar su persiana.

examples.en_text: Every morning, my grandfather opened up shop with enthusiasm to serve the neighbors.
examples.target_text: Cada mañana, mi abuelo levantaba su persiana con ilusión para atender a los vecinos.

examples.en_text: By nine in the morning, the clothing store has already opened for business.
examples.target_text: A las nueve de la mañana, la tienda de ropa ya ha levantado su persiana.

explanation_en: The pronominal passive 'respirarse' is used with abstract nouns like 'alivio', 'tensión', or 'miedo' to indicate that an atmosphere or feeling is palpable in the air. It translates to 'one can breathe/feel a certain...'. It is a highly literary yet common journalistic expression to describe the mood of a place.

examples.en_text: After handing in the final exam, a certain relief can be felt in the classroom.
examples.target_text: Después de entregar el examen final, se respira cierto alivio en el aula.

examples.en_text: When the doctor said the surgery had been a success, a certain relief was felt in the waiting room.
examples.target_text: Cuando el médico dijo que la operación había sido un éxito, se respiró cierto alivio en la sala de espera.

examples.en_text: Upon confirming that the company was not going to close, a certain relief could be felt among the employees.
examples.target_text: Al confirmarse que la empresa no iba a cerrar, se respiraba cierto alivio entre los empleados.

examples.en_text: Now that the storm has passed and the sky is clear, a certain relief can be felt in the town.
examples.target_text: Ahora que la tormenta ha pasado y el cielo está despejado, se respira cierto alivio en el pueblo.

examples.en_text: After signing the peace agreement, a certain relief could finally be felt throughout the region.
examples.target_text: Tras firmar el acuerdo de paz, por fin se respiraba cierto alivio en toda la región.

examples.en_text: Since they made up, a certain relief can be felt at family gatherings.
examples.target_text: Desde que hicieron las paces, se respira cierto alivio en las reuniones familiares.

explanation_en: 'Agridulce' (bittersweet) is a compound adjective combining 'agrio' (sour) and 'dulce' (sweet). When paired with 'sentimiento' or 'sabor', it describes a mixed emotion of happiness and sadness. The modifier 'un tanto' is a B2/C1 level way of saying 'somewhat' or 'rather'.

examples.en_text: Finishing university left me with a somewhat bittersweet feeling, as I say goodbye to my friends but start a new stage.
examples.target_text: Terminar la universidad me dejó un sentimiento un tanto agridulce, ya que me despido de mis amigos pero empiezo una nueva etapa.

examples.en_text: Selling my childhood home gives me a somewhat bittersweet feeling.
examples.target_text: Vender la casa de mi infancia me produce un sentimiento un tanto agridulce.

examples.en_text: His retirement party was a success, but we were all left with a somewhat bittersweet feeling due to his departure.
examples.target_text: Su fiesta de jubilación fue un éxito, pero todos nos quedamos con un sentimiento un tanto agridulce por su partida.

examples.en_text: The last day of vacation always gives me a somewhat bittersweet feeling because I have to go back to work.
examples.target_text: El último día de vacaciones siempre me genera un sentimiento un tanto agridulce porque tengo que volver al trabajo.

examples.en_text: The end of the movie left me with a somewhat bittersweet feeling; I didn't expect it to end like that.
examples.target_text: El final de la película me dejó un sentimiento un tanto agridulce; no esperaba que terminara así.

examples.en_text: Seeing my youngest son move out of the house is a somewhat bittersweet feeling for me.
examples.target_text: Ver a mi hijo menor mudarse de casa es un sentimiento un tanto agridulce para mí.

explanation_en: This idiomatic prepositional phrase means to be extremely close to something, either physically (at the threshold) or temporally (on the verge of happening). It is often used with verbs of movement or state like 'quedarse' or 'estar'. It is highly evocative and common in news reporting.

examples.en_text: With how cold it is today, it's clear that we are at the doorstep of winter.
examples.target_text: Con el frío que hace hoy, está claro que estamos a las puertas del invierno.

examples.en_text: After working thirty years at the company, my father is on the verge of retirement.
examples.target_text: Después de trabajar treinta años en la empresa, mi padre está a las puertas de la jubilación.

examples.en_text: The team played very well, but they fell just short of the final.
examples.target_text: El equipo jugó muy bien, pero se quedó a las puertas de la final.

examples.en_text: We are on the verge of final exams and the library is full of students.
examples.target_text: Estamos a las puertas de los exámenes finales y la biblioteca está llena de estudiantes.

examples.en_text: After signing this contract, the small company finds itself on the doorstep of international success.
examples.target_text: Tras firmar este contrato, la pequeña empresa se encuentra a las puertas del éxito internacional.

examples.en_text: Technology is changing so fast that we are on the threshold of a new digital era.
examples.target_text: La tecnología está cambiando tan rápido que estamos a las puertas de una nueva era digital.

explanation_en: This is a very common and versatile verbal locution meaning to confront, tackle, or cope with a difficult situation, expense, or enemy. It literally means 'to make a forehead to'. It always requires the preposition 'a' before the object.

examples.en_text: We have to face our problems instead of running away from them.
examples.target_text: Tenemos que hacer frente a nuestros problemas en lugar de huir de ellos.

examples.en_text: The company had to face a serious crisis last year.
examples.target_text: La empresa tuvo que hacer frente a una grave crisis el año pasado.

examples.en_text: How are we going to cope with these unexpected expenses?
examples.target_text: ¿Cómo vamos a hacer frente a estos gastos imprevistos?

examples.en_text: The government must address the lack of housing in the city.
examples.target_text: El gobierno debe hacer frente a la falta de vivienda en la ciudad.

examples.en_text: She is prepared to face any challenge in her new job.
examples.target_text: Ella está preparada para hacer frente a cualquier desafío en su nuevo trabajo.

examples.en_text: Together we can cope with the difficulties that arise.
examples.target_text: Juntos podemos hacer frente a las dificultades que surjan.

explanation_en: 'Convertido en' means 'turned into' or 'transformed into'. When paired with 'ceniza' (ash) or 'cenizas' (ashes), it is the standard Spanish equivalent of 'reduced to ashes'. It is used both literally (for fires) and figuratively (for ruined plans or dreams).

examples.en_text: After the huge forest fire, the beautiful pine trees were reduced to ashes.
examples.target_text: Después del gran incendio forestal, los hermosos pinos quedaron convertidos en ceniza.

examples.en_text: She burned her ex-boyfriend's letter and watched it turn to ash.
examples.target_text: Ella quemó la carta de su exnovio y la vio quedar convertida en ceniza.

examples.en_text: The city's old theater ended up reduced to ashes after last night's accident.
examples.target_text: El antiguo teatro de la ciudad acabó convertido en ceniza tras el accidente de anoche.

examples.en_text: All our family photos ended up turned to ash due to the short circuit.
examples.target_text: Todas nuestras fotos familiares terminaron convertidas en ceniza por culpa del cortocircuito.

examples.en_text: In a second, all his plans to open the restaurant were reduced to ashes.
examples.target_text: En un segundo, todos sus planes de abrir el restaurante quedaron convertidos en ceniza.

examples.en_text: By morning, the wooden log we put on the campfire had already turned to ash.
examples.target_text: Por la mañana, el tronco de madera que pusimos en la fogata ya se había convertido en ceniza.

idiom: la otra cara de la moneda
explanation_en: This is a direct equivalent of the English idiom 'the other side of the coin', used to introduce a contrasting situation or perspective. It is highly common in journalistic and argumentative Spanish. It is grammatically straightforward but essential for structuring comparisons naturally.

examples.en_text: Tourism brings a lot of money to the city, but the other side of the coin is the increase in rent prices.
examples.target_text: El turismo trae mucho dinero a la ciudad, pero la otra cara de la moneda es el aumento de los precios del alquiler.

examples.en_text: Working from home is very comfortable, but the other side of the coin is that sometimes you feel a bit lonely.
examples.target_text: Trabajar desde casa es muy cómodo, pero la otra cara de la moneda es que a veces te sientes un poco solo.

examples.en_text: Social networks allow us to stay connected, although the other side of the coin is the lack of privacy.
examples.target_text: Las redes sociales nos permiten estar conectados, aunque la otra cara de la moneda es la falta de privacidad.

examples.en_text: Being famous has many advantages, but the other side of the coin is that you lose your freedom.
examples.target_text: Ser famoso tiene muchas ventajas, pero la otra cara de la moneda es que pierdes tu libertad.

examples.en_text: Living abroad is a great experience, but the other side of the coin is missing your family.
examples.target_text: Vivir en el extranjero es una gran experiencia, pero la otra cara de la moneda es extrañar a tu familia.

examples.en_text: The company grew rapidly this year, but the other side of the coin was the team's accumulated stress.
examples.target_text: La empresa creció rápidamente este año, pero la otra cara de la moneda fue el estrés acumulado del equipo.

explanation_en: This collocation means to produce the desired effect, succeed, or bear fruit. Unlike English, which uses 'to yield' or 'to produce', Spanish uses the verb 'dar' (to give). It can be used in both singular ('dar resultado') and plural ('dar resultados').

examples.en_text: In the end, all our effort on the project has paid off.
examples.target_text: Al final, todo nuestro esfuerzo en el proyecto ha dado resultado.

examples.en_text: The medicines the doctor prescribed me have finally yielded results.
examples.target_text: Los medicamentos que me recetó el médico por fin han dado resultado.

examples.en_text: Studying a little bit every day has paid off, and I passed the exam.
examples.target_text: Estudiar un poco cada día ha dado resultado y he aprobado el examen.

examples.en_text: Do you think this new marketing strategy will yield results?
examples.target_text: ¿Crees que esta nueva estrategia de marketing dará resultado?

examples.en_text: Changing my eating habits has paid off, and I feel more energetic.
examples.target_text: Cambiar de hábitos alimenticios ha dado resultado y me siento con más energía.

examples.en_text: The team's hard training paid off, and we won the championship.
examples.target_text: El duro entrenamiento del equipo dio resultado y ganamos el campeonato.

explanation_en: Originally a military term for hand-to-hand combat, 'cuerpo a cuerpo' is used metaphorically to describe fighting a fire, disease, or problem directly and with intense physical effort. It functions as an adverbial or adjectival phrase. It emphasizes the close, dangerous nature of the struggle.

examples.en_text: The soldiers train daily for hand-to-hand combat.
examples.target_text: Los soldados entrenan diariamente para el combate cuerpo a cuerpo.

examples.en_text: In basketball, close-contact defense is key to preventing the opponent from scoring.
examples.target_text: En el baloncesto, la defensa cuerpo a cuerpo es clave para evitar que el rival anote.

examples.en_text: The political debate turned into a very intense head-to-head struggle between the candidates.
examples.target_text: El debate político se convirtió en un cuerpo a cuerpo muy intenso entre los candidatos.

examples.en_text: In ancient times, battles were almost always decided in hand-to-hand combat.
examples.target_text: En la antigüedad, las batallas se decidían casi siempre en el cuerpo a cuerpo.

examples.en_text: In the self-defense course, we learned techniques to defend ourselves in close quarters.
examples.target_text: En el curso de defensa personal aprendimos técnicas para defendernos cuerpo a cuerpo.

examples.en_text: The two companies are competing head-to-head to dominate the technology market.
examples.target_text: Las dos empresas compiten cuerpo a cuerpo por dominar el mercado tecnológico.
